anatomy.flutter: Nothing — Flutter has no standalone Label primitive at all. Its role is absorbed into FieldLabel (lib/src/components/ui/field.dart:537), which composes StyledText plus its own tap-activation logic directly rather than wrapping a separate Label widget the way FieldLabel on the web wraps <Label>.
anatomy.web: <LabelPrimitive.Root data-slot="label"> from Radix UI — a standalone, reusable <label> primitive that FieldLabel (components/ui/field.tsx) composes on top of, and that the label doc page shows being used bare, outside of Field, directly wired to a native input via htmlFor.
anatomy.note: origin: web-only — there is no Flutter Label primitive to be missing anything, by design. The web needs a standalone Label because HTML's accessible-name/click-to-focus association is id-based (htmlFor); Flutter has no id graph, so the same job is folded directly into FieldLabel's focus/activator plumbing instead of factored into a reusable non-field primitive. This is the correct platform split, not an unported component.

api.flutter: No Label API exists to compare — origin: web-only means there is nothing on the Flutter side to name props against.
api.web: Label is React.ComponentProps<typeof LabelPrimitive.Root> — effectively htmlFor plus any div/span prop passthrough, exactly what a native <label> accepts.
api.note: Per the audit brief's rule for origin: web-only rows, this dimension records what Flutter does instead rather than a missing counterpart: FieldLabel's own parameter list (text, spec, focusNode, activator, enabled, onTap — field.dart:538-546) is the functional equivalent of Label's htmlFor-driven API, expressed as explicit focus/activator wiring instead of an id-linked DOM attribute.

states.flutter: FieldLabel resolves disabled dimming and the group-aware styling itself, reading enabled and a FieldActivator/FocusNode off the enclosing FieldScope — there is no separate Label object with its own state to compare.
states.web: Label's class list carries group-data-[disabled=true]:pointer-events-none group-data-[disabled=true]:opacity-50 and peer-disabled:cursor-not-allowed peer-disabled:opacity-50 — two different CSS relational selectors (group vs peer) for the same 'the field I describe is disabled' state.
states.note: Flutter has no CSS-selector equivalent of group/peer, so FieldLabel reads the enclosing FieldScope's `enabled` directly (field.dart) rather than relying on a sibling/ancestor DOM relationship — a different mechanism producing the same visual dimming, which is the correct idiomatic substitution for a platform with no selector combinators.

disabled.flutter: FieldLabel.disabledOpacity = SurfaceOpacity.disabled is applied when the field it labels is disabled, per field.dart:593-594 — the label dims in step with its control without needing a group/peer relationship.
disabled.web: Label's own disabled dimming is entirely selector-driven (group-data-[disabled=true]:opacity-50 / peer-disabled:opacity-50) and requires the surrounding markup to declare data-disabled on a `group` ancestor or mark the input as a `peer` — a DOM-shape contract Label itself cannot enforce.
disabled.note: Both platforms dim the label exactly when its field is disabled; the web spells this as two alternative CSS relational selectors that depend on correct DOM nesting/ordering, while Flutter spells it as a direct FieldScope.enabled read with no such fragility — a platform-appropriate substitution, not a missing feature.

interaction.flutter: FieldLabel's doc comment (field.dart:520-536) lays out an explicit activation-precedence ladder — the caller's own onTap, then a registered FieldActivator callback, then a focus-node fallback, then no recognizer at all when neither exists — reproducing 'click the label, activate the control' without an id/for DOM relationship.
interaction.web: Label htmlFor="id" relies on the browser's native label-click-focuses-associated-control behaviour — clicking anywhere on the text moves focus (or toggles a checkbox) via the id/for linkage alone, no JS required.
interaction.note: The web gets click-to-activate for free from HTML's native label semantics; Flutter has no id graph to express `for=`, so FieldLabel reproduces the same click-to-activate behaviour explicitly through FieldActivator/FocusNode plumbing — functionally equivalent, mechanically necessary because the platform lacks the native primitive.

semantics.flutter: FieldLabel supplies the accessible name via whatever Semantics(label:) the enclosing field control reads (e.g. Input.label, InputOtp.label) rather than an id-based association — the label text becomes the control's own announced name.
semantics.web: LabelPrimitive.Root renders a real <label htmlFor>, so assistive technology gets the standard label/control association for free through the DOM's own accessibility tree — clicking or activating the label both focuses AND is announced as naming the control.
semantics.note: Both platforms end with the control announcing the label text as its accessible name; the web achieves it through native label-for-id association and Flutter achieves it by threading the label string directly into the control's own Semantics(label:) parameter — different mechanisms, equivalent outcome, and the correct answer for a platform with no DOM id graph.
